deck_context.source_summary: Class 19 follows the Sling Models, Model Exporter, OSGi services, configuration and servlet-boundary lessons. It teaches how focused JUnit 5 tests and AEM Mocks protect public model and service behavior with representative content, configuration and dependencies outside a running AEM SDK.
deck_context.core_claim: A useful unit test arranges the smallest representative AEM state, executes a public contract, asserts one observable behavior and is proven red before the minimum implementation makes it green.
revision_rules: Render exactly one fixed top-left eyebrow with the two-digit slide number and a short section label.
Preserve the accurate main diagram from the existing slide, then add concrete technical evidence and short why-it-matters annotations.
Use the canvas densely but legibly; only the Questions slide should retain generous open space.
Do not invent unrelated APIs, commands, tools, exercises or recap content.
canonical_facts: A unit test should protect observable public behavior rather than private implementation shape.
JUnit Jupiter uses @Test for test methods and @BeforeEach for fresh per-test setup.
AemContextExtension manages AEM mock context setup and cleanup for JUnit 5 tests.
AemContext exposes mock resource, request, response and OSGi facilities without starting an AEM SDK.
Tests should load only the content tree and register only the models, services or adapters required by the behavior.
Sling Models must be registered in the mock context when classpath discovery is not available.
ModelFactory.createModel throws useful model-creation exceptions while adaptTo may return null.
Configured, missing, invalid and intentionally supported legacy content are separate behavior contracts.
registerInjectActivateService injects dependencies, activates and registers a Declarative Services component in the mock OSGi environment.
AEM Mocks should represent platform boundaries it supports; small stubs or Mockito belong only at external or unsupported collaborator boundaries.
A mock-based unit test does not prove browser, deployment or full-runtime integration behavior.
A regression test should be observed failing when the protected behavior is absent before the minimum fix makes the same test pass.
After a focused test passes, the complete core test suite should run to detect neighboring regressions.

slides.title: A unit test protects behavior, not implementation shape.
slides.intent: Anchor every test in an externally observable contract that may regress.
key_points: Start with one behavior a consumer depends on.
Supply the smallest representative input.
Execute the public model or service contract.
Assert the observable result.
Do not couple tests to private methods or field layout.

local_context.required_background: Place INPUT, PUBLIC CONTRACT and OBSERVABLE RESULT inside the protected test boundary. Place PRIVATE METHODS, FIELD LAYOUT and INTERNAL CALL ORDER outside it. Use GuideCard.getTitle() or GuideUrlService.resolve() as compact public-contract examples, not both as full code listings.

layout.composition: A protected-contract boundary encloses input, public API and observable result; private implementation details sit outside as crossed-out test targets.
layout.intent: Make the test ownership boundary visible rather than presenting generic testing advice.

visual_elements.main_visual: Consumer contract boundary with valid and invalid assertion targets.

constraints: Render PUBLIC CONTRACT and OBSERVABLE RESULT exactly.
Show private methods and field layout outside the assertion boundary.
Do not imply implementation details may never be inspected while arranging an AEM test.

slides.title: Arrange, act and assert one behavior per failure.
slides.intent: Make a failing test small enough to diagnose without a custom testing abstraction.
key_points: ARRANGE representative content, configuration and dependencies.
ACT once through the public contract.
ASSERT one observable expectation.
Name the business state in the test method.
Keep shared setup genuinely shared.

local_context.required_background: Use one compact Java test specimen named returnsFallbackWhenTitleMissing(). Arrange selects /content/guides/missing-title, act creates GuideCard, assert checks the fallback title. Keep the code schematic and readable rather than syntactically exhaustive.

layout.composition: Three sequential zones labeled ARRANGE, ACT and ASSERT around one compact test specimen, ending in one readable failure message.
layout.intent: Teach the diagnostic rhythm of a focused test through one concrete example.

visual_elements.main_visual: Arrange-Act-Assert pipeline with a compact Guide Card fallback test.

constraints: Render ARRANGE, ACT and ASSERT exactly.
Show only one behavior and one primary assertion.
Do not create a reusable test-builder abstraction.

slides.title: JUnit 5 owns lifecycle, execution and assertions.
slides.intent: Introduce only the JUnit Jupiter pieces needed for a focused AEM unit test.
key_points: @Test marks an executable behavior check.
@BeforeEach prepares fresh common state.
@ExtendWith(AemContextExtension.class) connects mock lifecycle.
Use direct assertions: assertEquals, assertTrue, assertThrows.
Isolation matters more than clever fixtures.

local_context.required_background: Trace two independent test runs through EXTENSION SETUP → @BeforeEach → @Test → ASSERTION → CLEANUP. Show that each run receives fresh state. Do not include JUnit 4 rules or a large annotation catalog.

layout.composition: A horizontal JUnit lifecycle lane branches into two isolated test executions with fresh-state markers.
layout.intent: Make extension lifecycle and test isolation clearer than an annotation reference table.

visual_elements.main_visual: JUnit Jupiter lifecycle lane with two isolated test runs.

constraints: Render @Test, @BeforeEach and @ExtendWith(AemContextExtension.class) exactly.
Show setup and cleanup around each independent test.
Do not introduce @BeforeAll, parameterized tests or JUnit 4.

slides.title: AEM Mocks supplies only the AEM boundary the test needs.
slides.intent: Distinguish a fast in-memory unit-test environment from a running AEM instance.
key_points: AemContext exposes mock resource, request, response and OSGi facilities.
Load only the content tree required by the behavior.
Register only the models, services or adapters the unit consumes.
Choose one fitting resource-resolver mock type.
A passing mock test does not prove full-runtime integration.

local_context.required_background: Inside one bounded AemContext show MOCK CONTENT, RESOURCE RESOLVER, REQUEST/RESPONSE, MODEL REGISTRATION and OSGi REGISTRY. Outside the boundary show AEM SDK, DISPATCHER and BROWSER as not proven by this unit test.

layout.composition: A bounded AemContext architecture contains five mock facilities; a separate muted outer-runtime strip shows what the unit test does not prove.
layout.intent: Communicate both the usefulness and fidelity ceiling of AEM Mocks.

visual_elements.main_visual: In-memory AemContext boundary versus excluded full-runtime systems.

constraints: Render AemContext, MOCK CONTENT and OSGi REGISTRY exactly.
Keep AEM SDK, Dispatcher and browser outside the proven boundary.
Do not imply AEM Mocks implements every AEM API.

slides.title: Test configured, missing and invalid content as separate contracts.
slides.intent: Protect authoring fallbacks and validation decisions that keep rendering safe.
key_points: Configured content returns the authored, normalized value.
Missing optional content returns the documented fallback or empty state.
Invalid content is rejected, normalized or disabled by contract.
Legacy content stays safe only when compatibility is intentional.
Name each state in its test.

slides.title: Mock the platform boundary, not the code under test.
slides.intent: Prevent brittle tests that merely replay implementation calls.
key_points: Use real objects when they run cheaply in memory.
Use AEM Mocks for supported Sling, repository and OSGi boundaries.
Use a small stub or Mockito for an external or unsupported collaborator.
Stub public results, not internal call sequences.
Use integration tests when real runtime fidelity is required.

slides.title: Red → green proves the regression check.
slides.intent: Show that the focused test detects the missing behavior before it certifies the fix.
key_points: Run one named test with a focused Maven command.
Remove or bypass the Guide Card fallback and capture RED.
Restore the minimum behavior and rerun the same command GREEN.
Read the first useful failure before changing code.
Rerun the complete core test suite.

local_context.required_background: Use the exact command mvn -pl core -Dtest=GuideCardImplTest test. Show one loop: protected fallback absent → expected assertion failure RED → minimum fallback restored → same test GREEN → mvn -pl core test full-suite gate. The red state is intentional evidence, not a broken build left unresolved.

layout.composition: A terminal command anchors a four-stage red-to-green evidence loop ending in a full core-suite gate.
layout.intent: Make regression proof a visible workflow rather than a slogan.

visual_elements.main_visual: Focused Maven test moving through red failure, minimum fix, green pass and full-suite verification.

constraints: Render mvn -pl core -Dtest=GuideCardImplTest test exactly.
Show the same focused test in RED and GREEN.
Do not suggest committing or shipping the intentionally broken red state.

slides.intent: Consolidate the testing decisions developers should carry into Week 4 practice.

Exercise real adaptation or activation boundaries.
Prove the test red before accepting green evidence.
